Category 5 - Household, Public Health, A.one: Registration of pesticides used outside agriculture: household, public health, aircraft disinsection, ectoparasites and biocides.

pts: Household insecticides 5.1 · Public health programmes 5.2 · Aircraft 5.3
Mites, ticks, bedbugs and other ectoparasites 5.4 · Biocides incl. paints 5.5

5.1 Household insecticides.one: Data for indoor-use insecticides against ants, cockroaches, flies, mosquitoes, bedbugs, termites etc. (211th and 266th RC).
nums: maximum in a household combination (more only with a valid method)

pts: Only from technical registered under the Act; judged together with the technical data
Label name format: 'household pesticide containing x% w/w …'
Technical source and purity; full composition and ingredient properties
ATR from an independent national / international lab; shelf-life data
Process, effluent treatment, sample with standards, BIS residue method
Brief directions on the label; detailed uses, insects, dosage and places in the leaflet
Restricted-use products: say 'For … use only' in capitals

watch: Label and leaflet must say: 'Not to be used on any food crop'

5.2 Public Health Programme.one: Data for insecticides used in government vector-control (public health) programmes u/s 9(3).
nums: multi-centric bio-efficacy by ICMR / MoHFW institutes

pts: Bio-efficacy as per ICMR Common Protocol for Public Health Pesticides (2023)
WHOPES-recommended insecticides: Phase I data exempted (449th RC)
Recommendation from the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme
Toxicity: six acute studies, birds and fish
Six acute studies on the premix, plus health monitoring of users with the final product

5.3 Aircraft disinfection.one: Data for insecticides used to disinsect aircraft (280th RC, 2007).
nums: national / NABL labs, at least 2 trials each

pts: Only from registered technical; sample analysed at CIL Faridabad
ATR from an independent lab; shelf-life data; BIS method where available
Persistence on aircraft surfaces and concentration in air, in 3 labs
Six acute studies plus health monitoring of spray crew and/or volunteers on board

watch: Label: 'Not to be used on any food as well as crops'

5.4 Ectoparasites (mites, bedbugs, ticks.one: Data for insecticides against ectoparasites such as mites, ticks and bedbugs, for technical and formulation (301st RC, 2009).

pts: Full chemistry for technical and formulation; shelf-life data except 9(3B) technical
Supplier authorisation, GLP / ISO report with first consignment, sample with standards
Formulation: persistence on treated surfaces; residues in bird organs, edible products and excreta
Bird studies include blood profile, enzymology and 15-day egg production records
Transport packaging specification must include the UN number

watch: Formulation import without registered technical: submit the full technical data too

5.5 Biocides & Biocide products (MUP); p.one: Registration of biocides and biocide products, incl. preservatives used in paints (389th RC, 2018).
nums: carbendazim: toxic labels; sale to professionals only

pts: No, if the biocide only protects the paint itself and no anti-microbial / insect claims are made
Yes for the biocide itself (technical or product) used as in-can or dry-film preservative
Only CIB&RC-registered biocide technicals may be used
Product without registered technical: declare source and give full technical data
All toxicology GLP-compliant; efficacy per ASTM 5589 / 5590 or CIB&RC protocols

watch: Carbendazim above 1000 ppm needs skull-and-crossbones and dead-fish/tree labels, 'Mutagen Cat 2', 'Reprotox Cat 2'
